installer.notice.title: FaceLogin 1.9.0 Update Notes
installer.notice.unknownCapture: Unknown-face capture (optional): when an unmatched face appears at the lock screen, a photo and event record are saved and can be browsed/deleted from the Console logs page (stored locally only)
installer.notice.coldBootKey: Key-triggered sign-in at boot (optional): by default recognition starts automatically at boot; you can change it to require any key press (same as lock screen)
installer.notice.threshold: Match threshold recalibrated 0.65 → 0.75: unlock failures caused by changing ambient light (e.g. moving between rooms) are significantly improved; stranger rejection is unaffected
installer.notice.usbCamera: Built-in USB camera frame-rate fix: prefers compressed formats, stable 30fps at 720p, face enrollment no longer stalls
installer.notice.firstAuto: Cold boot auto-recognizes only once: after a failed/timed-out attempt, or after switching to another tile and back, a key press is required to start recognition again
installer.notice.noLoop: Failed recognition no longer restarts the camera in a loop; switching to the password tile stops recognition immediately and password input is no longer interrupted
installer.notice.pinReset: Fixed the camera repeatedly activating and PIN appearing unavailable when resetting a Microsoft account PIN
installer.notice.msaDetection: Fixed Console still showing a local account after switching/linking to a Microsoft account
installer.notice.thresholdUpgrade: Fixed the match threshold not being synced to the new default after an upgrade install
installer.notice.facesPreserved: Already enrolled face data is unaffected; no re-enrollment needed

console.settings.title: System Settings
console.settings.autoApply: Changes are pushed to the background service automatically; no restart needed.
console.settings.rotationHelp: Use this when the camera is physically mounted in a non-standard orientation (e.g. vertical display). The preview reflects the rotation immediately.
console.settings.cameraHelp: When multiple or virtual cameras exist, choose the one used for enrollment and login.
console.settings.glasses: Glasses mode (enable when glasses make blink detection unstable)
console.settings.glassesHelp: Glasses mode uses adaptive blink detection that is more robust to frames/reflections, but may be less stable than the default mode. Keep it off unless needed.
console.settings.lowLight: Low-light enhancement (enable when recognition is unstable in dark environments)
console.settings.lowLightHelp: Normalizes brightness of dark face images to improve recognition and anti-spoof pass rates in low light. No effect in normal lighting. Keep it off unless needed.
console.settings.exposureControl: Face exposure auto-control (enable when over/under-exposure makes recognition unstable)
console.settings.exposureControlHelp: Automatically keeps face brightness in a target range: prefers the camera's hardware exposure/gain, falling back to digital gain when unsupported. Enrollment and unlock share the same target, so changing rooms or lighting no longer noticeably affects recognition. Re-enroll your face after enabling.
console.settings.memory: Memory optimization (release models after recognition to reduce background memory)
console.settings.memoryHelp: Releases the face models after recognition, dropping the service's background memory from ~60 MB to ~20 MB. Models auto-reload on the next unlock (~0.2–0.5 s). Enable on memory-sensitive devices.
console.settings.unknownFaces: Record unmatched faces (save photo and record when a stranger appears at the lock screen)
console.settings.unknownFacesHelp: When enabled, failed lock-screen matches save the frame and an event record under the data\unknown folder. Keeps up to 100 photos, stored locally only and never uploaded. Involves other people's facial images — enable with care.
console.settings.coldBootKey: Require a key press to trigger face recognition at boot (off by default: auto-recognize at boot)
console.settings.coldBootKeyHelp: When enabled, the sign-in screen at boot waits for any key press before starting recognition. For users who don't want the camera turning on automatically at boot.
console.settings.antiSpoofHelp: Lower = more lenient (easier to pass), higher = stricter (harder to pass). Default 0.30.
console.settings.matchHelp: Higher = stricter (the face must be more similar to pass). Default 60.
